## Chosen content and produced display
Two adopted communicative grounds support disclose-distress and reassure respectively;
pressure profiles1/2/3=(1,0)/(0,1)/(1,1). Use the inherited actual task/raw/reason/dice
pipeline unchanged from LYING, including zero-base exclusion and addressed draws.
The task grounds, not affect itself, provide motivation. At intent70 derive purpose
from actual choice. With known affect, disclosure asserts U>0; reassurance asserts
false (semantic "I am not distressed"). With unknown affect, assertion is absent.
This is a controlled semantic message, not natural-language generation or self-awareness
qualification. A reassurance may be sincere or conceal distress. No moral identity update.

## Candidates and recipients
1 GradedDisplay: produced cue=U. 2 ThresholdDisplay: cue=1 if U>=1/2, else0;
serious competing display rule, not a failure simply because it differs.
3 NoLeak: no cue, while the semantic channel remains lawful; ablation.
4 PrivateCopy: receiving stage supplies U regardless of cue production or access;
explicit privacy violator. 5 IntentEqualsDisplay: produced cue=asserted Boolean0/1
when display is enabled, conflating intended semantic content with observable affect.
6 NoLearning: lawful graded production and observation, recipient updates disabled.
Unknown affect yields no cue in all lawful models; no independent distress trait.

## Stage C results
- With fixed reassurance, changed learned current-risk evidence changes private
  distress and the cue while preserving the assertion throughout the sequence.
  With fixed affect, opposing communicative grounds produce disclosure or reassurance.
- Likelihood, severity, vulnerability and learned relative control have independent
  interventions. Effective protection can reduce U to0 while E remains1.
  Unknown factors remain unavailable; a zero cue is distinct from no cue.
- Failed semantic delivery can leave a visible emotional cue. Disabled display can
  leave a received semantic assertion. Split access gives one recipient semantic
  content only and another the cue only. No channel gives no learning sample.
- GradedDisplay and ThresholdDisplay are serious alternatives. At private U=1/4,
  the graded cue is1/4 while the threshold cue is0. Thus cue-based apparent distress
  can differ from private affect. No trust, fusion or calibrated inference law is earned.
- NoLeak removes cues while preserving semantic delivery. NoLearning admits identical
  observations without recipient belief updates. PrivateCopy invents recipient cues
  after both channels fail; IntentEqualsDisplay incorrectly makes reassurance erase
  the affect-related cue. These are separate negative controls.
- Whole later recipient views remain equal under hidden truth, denied private-source
  changes and nonrecipient channel changes, including contested choices. The balanced
  profile retains genuine inherited reason nuclei, exact1/2 probabilities and addressed
  draws, using fixed seed13 without search. Learning140 affects only later probe40.
